name: San Diego
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching San Diego: defense contractor and life sciences diligence, Baja California research and litigation.
hero_lede: San Diego joins a dense military and defense economy, a top life sciences cluster and the busiest land border with Mexico. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, coordinating California-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: San Diego is the second largest city in California, with about 1.38 million residents in July 2022 according to Census estimates cited by the city, at the centre of a county of about 3.3 million. Defense dominates the regional economy: the city's own profile cites a 2022 study attributing about 56.2 billion dollars, or 24.5 percent of gross regional product, to defense-related activity. The deepwater port hosts major naval facilities and the West Coast's main naval shipbuilding yards. Life sciences employed about 77,000 people in 2022, concentrated in La Jolla and Sorrento Valley, alongside wireless and semiconductor technology led by Qualcomm. Other headquarters include Sempra, Illumina, Viasat, Dexcom and General Atomics.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to San Diego because government contracts, scientific intellectual property and cross-border trade all converge there. Defense primes and subcontractors need assurance about suppliers, ownership and foreign influence. Investors and acquirers in biotech and medical devices need to test founders, data and patent claims. The San Ysidro and Otay Mesa crossings link San Diego with Tijuana and the Baja California maquiladora base, where more than 1,100 companies operate under Mexico's IMMEX programme, so supply chain, customs and counterparty questions often span two legal systems. Litigation in California state courts and the federal Southern District of California brings further demand for factual research.

matters.title: Defense supplier and ownership diligence
matters.text: San Diego's defense primes depend on layered subcontractor networks. We research supplier ownership, affiliates and foreign links, debarment and litigation history, and the backgrounds of key principals, helping contractors assess integrity and foreign ownership questions before awarding subcontracts, teaming agreements or acquisitions.

matters.title: Biotech and medical device investment
matters.text: Investors in La Jolla and Sorrento Valley companies rely on claims about science, patents and people. We review founders' and executives' histories, prior company outcomes, litigation, regulatory actions and patent assignments, testing representations before financing, licensing or acquisition.

matters.title: Cross-border supply chain counterparties
matters.text: Many San Diego companies source from or manufacture in Tijuana and wider Baja California. We research Mexican and US counterparties, their ownership and litigation history, and links between intermediaries, coordinating Mexican counsel and professionals where records or enquiries in Mexico are required.

matters.title: Trade secret and employee departures
matters.text: Engineers and scientists move frequently between San Diego technology and biotech employers. Where confidential information may have left with a departing employee, we research new ventures, entity formations, patent filings and public statements so counsel can assess claims, using lawful public sources only.

matters.title: Litigation and asset research
matters.text: We support counsel in San Diego Superior Court and federal cases with witness and party backgrounds, corporate history and asset research across California, other states and, where relevant, Mexico, so that pleadings, settlement positions and enforcement plans rest on verified facts.

local_context.title: Courts in San Diego
local_context.text: The Superior Court of California, County of San Diego, hears civil and commercial litigation in the county, with appeals to the California Court of Appeal, Fourth Appellate District, Division One, which sits in San Diego. Federal fraud, securities, government contracts, patent and commercial matters are heard in the US District Court for the Southern District of California, headquartered in the city. Counsel selects the forum, and we tailor research to its rules and records.

local_context.title: California investigator licensing
local_context.text: California regulates private investigators under the Private Investigator Act, Business and Professions Code sections 7512 to 7573, administered by the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services within the Department of Consumer Affairs. Anyone conducting covered investigations for consideration needs a licence unless an exemption applies; attorneys are exempt only when acting as attorneys, and investigators they hire must still be licensed. Unlicensed practice is a misdemeanour. TDSC coordinates BSIS-licensed professionals for California work.

local_context.title: California privacy and recording rules
local_context.text: California's privacy framework is stricter than most states. Its Penal Code generally requires consent of all parties to record confidential communications, and its consumer privacy law gives residents rights over personal information held by many businesses. Investigative plans for San Diego matters are reviewed with counsel against these rules before any interviews, recordings or data collection, and pretexting is never used.

local_context.title: Records and the Mexican border
local_context.text: California entities are registered with the Secretary of State, whose filings include statements of information listing officers or managers. San Diego County's Assessor, Recorder and County Clerk holds property records. Records about Tijuana and Baja California companies, property and litigation sit in Mexican registries and courts under different access rules, so cross-border research is scoped with Mexican counsel and coordinated with appropriately qualified local professionals.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in San Diego and works on San Diego matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's counsel first, whether a defense supplier review, a life sciences investment, a cross-border counterparty question, a trade secret concern or litigation support, and scope research to it. Sources include California Secretary of State and county records, Superior Court and Southern District of California dockets, federal contracting and debarment records, patent and regulatory filings, and media. Work in Mexico is scoped with Mexican counsel. Any fieldwork in California is carried out by BSIS-licensed investigators, with California's recording and privacy rules reviewed in advance. Reports identify sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a California licence to work in San Diego?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. The Private Investigator Act requires anyone who conducts covered investigations for consideration to hold a licence from the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services, unless an exemption applies. Investigators hired by attorneys must still be licensed. TDSC does not hold a California licence and coordinates BSIS-licensed professionals for local work.

faqs.q: Can you research companies in Tijuana or Baja California?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. We review publicly available Mexican and US records, media and trade data, and coordinate Mexican counsel and appropriately qualified local professionals where enquiries or registry searches in Mexico are needed. Mexican records follow different access rules, so we agree scope and expected coverage with the client before work begins.

faqs.q: How do you vet a defense subcontractor in San Diego?
faqs.a: We identify the company's owners, parents and affiliates, including any foreign links, then review federal contracting and exclusion records, litigation, regulatory actions and principals' backgrounds. Findings help prime contractors and acquirers assess integrity and foreign ownership questions. We do not access classified or restricted government systems; research is limited to lawful sources.

faqs.q: Can conversations be recorded during a San Diego investigation?
faqs.a: California generally requires the consent of all parties to record confidential communications, which is stricter than many states. TDSC does not record conversations without a clear legal basis confirmed by counsel and never uses pretexting. Interview plans for California matters are reviewed with counsel before any contact is made.

faqs.q: What do you check before investing in a San Diego biotech company?
faqs.a: We review founders' and executives' prior companies and outcomes, litigation, bankruptcies, regulatory actions and media, and confirm patent ownership and assignments through public filings. We compare findings with representations in diligence materials. Scientific validity is a matter for technical experts; our work addresses people, ownership and track record.
